title: Nashville Hot Chicken Tender Sandwich
summary: Buttermilk-marinated chicken breast strips, crunchy-dredged, fried and tossed in cayenne spice oil, stacked on butter-toasted brioche with herby ranch, pickles and a creamy cabbage slaw.
notes: Video: 'Perfect Nashville Hot Fried Chicken At Home (2 Ways)' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). This file is one of two versions in the video (house rule 6), both pointing to the same transcript: the classic bone-in leg quarters on white toast, and a boneless tender sandwich. Written recipe for both: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/perfect-nashville-hot-fried-chicken-at-home-2-ways-recipe (serves 4, prep 30 min, cook 45 min for the page as a whole). Marinating time is not in prep_minutes (house rule 13): at least 2 hours, ideally overnight. The page gives a separate marinade for each version but one dredge and one hot-oil mix; the video says the tenders are breaded 'exactly like the leg quarters' and tossed in the spicy oil, so this file repeats the full dredge and hot oil so it stands alone. All marinade, dredge and hot-oil amounts are stated in the video and match the page. House rules applied: the buttermilk marinade is poured off and excluded; the dredge counts at 25%; the deep-frying oil is excluded and absorbed oil is counted at 10% of the raw breaded weight (arithmetic on that line). The hot spice oil (about 1 cup of the frying oil whisked into the spices) is a dunking oil made in a bigger batch than stays on the chicken and no share is stated, so every hot-oil line counts at 25% (house rule 10; full batch kept in each line's text). Optional chicken bouillon powder is counted (at 25%) because the transcript narrates it being added with the other spices (house rule 11); this is inferred from the narration, not seen on screen. The optional extra spoonful of spice oil is excluded (mentioned, not added). The cayenne in the hot oil can go up to 1/2 cup; we use 1/4 cup. Potato starch is listed as an excluded alternative to the cornstarch. Smoked paprika uses the existing paprika slug. Brown sugar is dark brown (light is allowed). Version 2 (tender sandwich): 4 servings, from the 4 buns the video asks for ('you'll need four for this recipe') and the page's 4 servings. The ranch batch (about 1 1/3 cups) is bigger than what he spreads on the 4 sandwiches: he says it keeps a couple of days and gives no amount per bun, so 50% of each ranch line is counted (house rule 10). The slaw is made for the sandwiches and piled on in full, so it counts in full. Buns: he lists burger bun, brioche or potato rolls; we use brioche, as the written recipe does (the existing hamburger-bun slug is whole-wheat, which does not fit), with a USDA plain hamburger roll proxy and 65 g per bun as our estimate. Our estimates: 1 Tbsp butter to toast the buns, about 120 g sliced dill pickles, 1/2 tsp salt each in the ranch batch (1/4 tsp counted) and the slaw (house rule 4). Black pepper to taste is not counted. Slaw vinegar: he says '2 tbsp or 20 g'; 2 Tbsp is closer to 30 g, so we keep the tablespoons. Prep and cook times are the page's figures for both versions together.

steps.text: Whisk the buttermilk, Frank's RedHot, salt and MSG for the marinade.
Cut the chicken breasts lengthwise into strips about 1/2 inch thick (thinner is fine). Massage them in the marinade, cover and refrigerate, ideally overnight.
Whisk the dredge: flour, cornstarch, salt, MSG, smoked paprika, cayenne and garlic powder.
In a heatproof bowl, whisk the hot-oil spices: cayenne, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, brown sugar and bouillon powder. Set aside.

For the ranch, combine the mayo and sour cream with the grated garlic and the finely chopped parsley and dill. Thin with about 1 Tbsp buttermilk to a thick, spreadable sauce and season with salt and pepper. It keeps a couple of days in the fridge.

Bread the strips as for the leg quarters: flick some marinade into the dredge to make clumps, press the flour onto each strip on all sides and shake off the excess. Fry in batches at 350°F for 3-5 minutes, until golden and 165°F inside.
Ladle about 1 cup of the hot frying oil into the spice mix and whisk. Toss the tenders in the spice oil as soon as they come out of the fryer, then drain on a wire rack.
Just before assembling, toss the sliced cabbage with the mayo, salt, sugar, cider vinegar and pepper by hand until evenly coated. Don't make it ahead or it goes soggy.
Toast the buns in butter. Spread ranch on the bottom buns, add pickles, 2-3 tenders and a mound of slaw, then close with a ranch-spread top bun.
